# The Pritiraj Review — Pritiraj & Partners

> 42 long-form, evidence-led essays on how India is governed, how it delivers, and what its next decades demand. Written by Pritiraj Brahma, Founding Partner, Pritiraj & Partners (Bengaluru, India). Published most weeks since 1 February 2026.

The firm’s stand: politics is the promise, governance is the delivery. India’s failures are failures of institutional design — tasks without owners, targets without deadlines, results nobody is required to publish — not failures of ambition or resources.

Every figure is attributed in-text to the instrument and release that produced it (PIB, RBI, CAG, NJDG, PRS, NCRB, MoSPI, the Economic Survey, a parliamentary reply, or a named report). Where sources conflict, the essay says so rather than choosing silently. Each essay carries a provenance line stating publication and revision dates, and where the argument rests on a dated series, the vintage of that series.

Every essay follows one structure: a blockquote lede, a numbered set of findings, analysis sections, an explicit counter-case, and a prescriptive "What we would do" close.

## How the Review is made

The essays are a by-product of the firm’s practice, not a separate research operation: the firm reads the ground picture on government initiatives daily and briefs leaders from it, and an essay follows where a pattern in those notes holds across states and years and the evidence is already on the record. Figures are verified against the primary document, an official statistical release (MoSPI, RBI, NSS), a PIB or ministry note, or a parliamentary reply, with two independent sources wherever practicable; reporting is labelled as reporting where no primary source is public. AI tools assist in structuring an argument once its evidence is assembled and built this site; they are not used to source facts, and every figure is verified by the author. Errors are corrected, marked as revised with the date, and the correction states what changed. Full method note: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/pritiraj-brahma/#method

- [Series](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/series/): multi-part analyses.
- [The Civics Series](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/civics/): a free five-chart reference on how India is governed — the org structure of the Union and a state, how a Prime Minister or Chief Minister is chosen, how a bill becomes law, the two paths a citizen can take into government (the examination and the ballot), and why a democracy keeps a permanent civil service. Roles only, no officeholders named, so it stays accurate between elections. Descriptive reference, not argument; the Review carries the argument.
- [Pritiraj Brahma](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/pritiraj-brahma/): author page, including the method note.

## Series

- [The Fiscal Settlement](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/series/the-fiscal-settlement/): three essays on where money sits in the Indian federation — Union to states, states to cities, and the dependent states.
- [The Degree Settlement](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/series/the-degree-settlement/): five essays on how India expanded higher education without building the ledger — who supplies the seats, who teaches in them, who certifies them, who leaves, and whether the degree reaches a job.

## Essays (newest first)

- [Thirty Thousand Crore, One Line — Who Creates Knowledge in Indian Higher Education](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/thirty-thousand-crore-one-line/) — Education & Skills, 28 August 2026, 13 min read. India’s higher education institutions spent ₹30,909 crore on research in 2023-24, up from ₹9,942 crore four years earlier — the fastest-growing segment of national R&D. That line covers public and private institutions together, with no published split. The state opened its research funding to private universities, withdrew the UGC-CARE list, and never built the register that would show which institutions create knowledge and which only count it.
- [The Degree and the Job — What the Apprenticeship Numbers Actually Say](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-degree-and-the-job/) — Education & Skills, 28 August 2026, 10 min read. Apprentices engaged under NAPS rose from 3.08 lakh in 2020-21 to 9.85 lakh in 2024-25 — real growth, set against 4.33 crore students in higher education. Two ministries run one statute, two evaluations report employment on incompatible definitions, and nobody publishes the number that matters: how many apprentices hold a job a year later.
- [The Students Who Leave — The Outflow, Its Measurement, and the Campuses Built to Answer It](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-students-who-leave/) — Education & Skills, 27 August 2026, 10 min read. Departures for study abroad fell from about 8.94 lakh in 2023 to 6.26 lakh in 2025 — a fall produced by visa policy in four other countries, not by anything India did. Asked what these students spend, the government told Parliament it does not maintain the information. Four foreign campuses now operate here under two regulators, and neither publishes what any of them enrolled.
- [Who Grades the Grader — Accreditation After the Arrests](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/who-grades-the-grader/) — Education & Skills, 25 August 2026, 9 min read. On 1 February 2025 the CBI arrested the chairman and six members of a NAAC inspection committee. The FIR describes ₹1.8 crore sought for a score above 3.65 and an A++ grade. Nearly 900 assessors were then removed. The response treated the assessors as the fault. The fault is in a design that makes a grade worth buying and cheap to sell.
- [The Post Nobody Filled — Faculty Vacancy as the Binding Constraint](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-post-nobody-filled/) — Education & Skills, 23 August 2026, 11 min read. As on 31 January 2025, 56.18 per cent of professor posts across India's central higher education institutions were vacant, on the Parliamentary Standing Committee's own figures. The shortage inverts the academic pyramid — worst at the top, worst again in reserved categories — and the ministry's position is that recruitment is not its responsibility.
- [Where the Seats Came From — Private Supply and the Regulator That Did Not Follow](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/where-the-seats-came-from/) — Education & Skills, 21 August 2026, 10 min read. Between 2014-15 and 2021-22 India added 408 universities and about 7,000 colleges. On the Ministry of Education's own returns, 65.3 per cent of responding colleges are private un-aided. The expansion was overwhelmingly private. The architecture built to supervise it was designed for a public system.
- [Fifty-Eight Thousand, Eight Hundred and Eighty-One — Manipur’s Displaced and the Border Policy Above Them](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/fifty-eight-thousand-eight-hundred-and-eighty-one/) — National Security, 19 August 2026, 10 min read. Manipur’s Home Department puts the displaced at 58,881 and the relief camps still open at 174. Above them, India has scrapped a working border rule and replaced it with a fence less than two per cent built and a pass system two neighbouring states administer differently.
- [Ten Lakh Uniforms and Three Different Answers — India's Internal Security Manpower Problem](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/ten-lakh-uniforms-and-three-different-answers/) — National Security, 19 August 2026, 10 min read. Parliament was told this year that the central armed police forces are short of 93,139 people, and also that they are short of 61,738. The same reply implies 69,246. A state that cannot state its own vacancy cannot plan its own recruitment.
- [The Village Is the Claim — India Is Building Its Northern Border and Not Counting Who Lives There](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-village-is-the-claim/) — National Security, 16 August 2026, 10 min read. The Vibrant Villages Programme exists to reverse outmigration from the villages along the China frontier. Four years in, the state publishes roads sanctioned, bridges approved and activities held. It does not publish how many people live in those villages.
- [The Sanction Is Not the Squadron — India's Defence Money Now Moves; Its Timelines Do Not](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-sanction-is-not-the-squadron/) — National Security, 16 August 2026, 10 min read. India's defence budget has crossed ₹7.84 lakh crore and, for the first time in years, the capital account was spent almost in full. The binding constraint has moved from money to time — and time is the one variable the system does not publish.
- [Two Surveys, One Country](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/two-surveys-one-country/) — Health & Human Development, 9 August 2026, 9 min read. India’s two official sources on child undernutrition disagree about wasting by fourteen percentage points. One of them is now used to report progress, and it is not the one designed to measure it.
- [Eight Hundred and Fifty Seats — What Delimitation Actually Decides](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/eight-hundred-and-fifty-seats-what-delimitation-actually-decides/) — Institutions & Reform, 8 August 2026, 11 min read. The Delimitation Bill, 2026 proposes a 850-member Lok Sabha with 272 seats reserved for women. The seat count is the least consequential thing about it.
- [The Arithmetic That Should Alarm Us — India's Learning Crisis as a Solvency Problem](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/india-learning-crisis-the-arithmetic-that-should-alarm-us/) — Governance & Delivery, 30 July 2026, 10 min read. India enrols nearly every child and half leave unable to do grade-level mathematics. Why the learning crisis is now a fiscal question — and the five structural corrections it requires.
- [Who Owns an Examination](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/who-owns-an-examination-the-reform-architecture-after-neet/) — Institutions & Reform, 26 July 2026, 8 min read. A minister resigned over an exam leak. The architecture that produced the leak — an agency with no statutory parent, no published error rate and no owner of record — was left exactly as it was.
- [The Dashboard Problem — When Measurement Replaces Delivery](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-dashboard-problem/) — Governance & Delivery, 23 July 2026, 9 min read. India has more real-time government dashboards than any comparable state. Pendency, learning outcomes and delivery gaps have not moved with them. Visibility is not accountability.
- [The District Is Where the State Lives — The Tier India Refuses to Staff](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-district-is-where-the-state-lives/) — State Capacity, 16 July 2026, 10 min read. India debates the Centre and the states endlessly and ignores the tier where governance actually succeeds or fails. The district runs at 19% IAS vacancy against a mandate that expands every year.
- [The Forty-One Percent Illusion — State Finances After the Sixteenth Commission](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-forty-one-percent-illusion-state-finances-after-the-sixteenth-finance-commission/) — Political Economy, 2 July 2026, 10 min read. The 16th Finance Commission held devolution at 41% and discontinued revenue deficit grants. Why a headline of continuity conceals the tightest state fiscal settlement in a decade.
- [The Certificate Is Not the Job — Why India Skills Millions and Employs Few](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-certificate-is-not-the-job/) — Governance & Delivery, 25 June 2026, 11 min read. PMKVY trained 13.7 million people in seven years and placed 18 per cent of them. The failure is not effort; it is a system built to count certificates instead of livelihoods.
- [The Campus Economy — India's Quietest Special Economic Zones](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-campus-economy-india-s-quietest-special-economic-zones/) — Political Economy, 18 June 2026, 13 min read. Roughly 37% of notified SEZ land is in use. Meanwhile four university gates have built the concentrated capital, talent and IP pools that SEZ policy spent twenty years trying to engineer.
- [India's Demographic Clock — The Deadline Beneath Every Other Debate](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/india-s-demographic-clock/) — Political Economy, 11 June 2026, 9 min read. A median age of 28 in an ageing world is India's greatest advantage and its deadline. The working-age share peaks in the 2040s; everything else is a question of what gets delivered before then.
- [Four Codes, Thirty-Six Rulebooks — The Labour Reform That Is Not Yet a Reform](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/four-codes-thirty-six-rulebooks-the-labour-reform-that-is-not-yet-a-reform/) — Governance & Delivery, 4 June 2026, 9 min read. Twenty-nine central labour laws were repealed on 21 November 2025. The central rules arrived on 8 May 2026. The states are where the reform is now decided.
- [The Northeast Is Not the Periphery — A Gateway That Is Not Yet Open](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-northeast-india-is-not-the-periphery/) — Federalism & the Northeast, 28 May 2026, 10 min read. Over ₹6 lakh crore committed in a decade, and the region's exports fell from $50.8m to $47.6m. The gateway framing is right; the execution gap is the whole problem.
- [The Tariff That Was Never Lawful — What India Conceded, and What It Should Learn](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-tariff-that-was-never-lawful-what-india-conceded-and-what-it-learned/) — Political Economy, 14 May 2026, 8 min read. India negotiated relief from a 50% US tariff in February 2026. Three weeks later the US Supreme Court held the instrument behind it was never authorised. A lesson in negotiating against legal durability.
- [The Specialist Who Was Never Sanctioned](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-specialist-who-was-never-sanctioned/) — State Capacity, 10 May 2026, 9 min read. The specialist shortfall at India’s rural community health centres appeared to shrink by a third this year. The number of specialists barely moved. The requirement was rewritten.
- [Cities Without Money — The Third Tier and the Capacity It Lacks](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/cities-without-money-the-third-tier-and-the-capacity-it-lacks/) — State Capacity, 7 May 2026, 10 min read. India's cities produce roughly 60% of GDP and raise 0.6% of it. The Sixteenth Commission has now sent them ₹3.6 lakh crore against conditions most cannot yet meet.
- [The Thirty-Nine Percent Question — Health Spending and What It Buys](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-thirty-nine-percent-question-health-spending-and-what-it-buys/) — Governance & Delivery, 30 April 2026, 9 min read. Out-of-pocket health spending has fallen from 62.6% to around 39%. Public health spending sits at 1.8% of GDP against a 2.5% target. Both numbers describe the same unfinished settlement.
- [Who Regulates the Regulators](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/who-regulates-the-regulators/) — Institutions & Reform, 23 April 2026, 11 min read. India built independent regulators for its most important sectors and then left their appointments, budgets and accountability inside the ministries they were meant to check.
- [Airsheds Do Not Respect District Lines](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/airsheds-do-not-respect-district-lines/) — Resources & Climate, 16 April 2026, 8 min read. India measures air pollution by city and manages it by municipality. The pollution arrives from a region several hundred kilometres wide. The mismatch is the whole problem.
- [Three in Four](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/three-in-four/) — Justice & Liberty, 12 April 2026, 8 min read. India’s prison population fell in 2023 and overcrowding eased by ten points. Nearly three-quarters of those inside have still not been convicted of anything.
- [The Missing Middle of Indian Enterprise](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-missing-middle-of-indian-enterprise/) — Political Economy, 9 April 2026, 13 min read. Only 14% of India's MSMEs have formal credit, against a gap estimated between ₹25 and ₹30 lakh crore. Indian firms stay small because staying small is the rational response to the system around them.
- [The Discom Turnaround — and What It Does Not Yet Prove](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-discom-turnaround-and-what-it-does-not-yet-prove/) — State Capacity, 2 April 2026, 9 min read. India's power distributors posted a collective profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 against accumulated losses of ₹6.47 lakh crore. A real turnaround, and a small one.
- [The Aquifer Is the Real Budget Constraint](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-aquifer-is-the-real-budget-constraint/) — Resources & Climate, 26 March 2026, 6 min read. India extracts 247.22 BCM of groundwater a year — a quarter of the world's total. 730 assessment units are over-exploited. The binding constraint on Indian agriculture is not credit or price.
- [Five Crore Cases and the Arithmetic of Delay](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/five-crore-cases-and-the-arithmetic-of-delay/) — Institutions & Reform, 19 March 2026, 9 min read. India's courts carry more than 5 crore pending cases with roughly 14 judges per million people against a recommended 50. The backlog is not a moral failing; it is a capacity equation.
- [Citizens Who Move, Entitlements That Do Not](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/citizens-who-move-entitlements-that-do-not/) — Governance & Delivery, 12 March 2026, 8 min read. India built a portable ration card and stopped there. A migrant worker still cannot vote, see a doctor, enrol a child or claim a pension where they actually live.
- [Sixty-Eight Paise in the Rupee](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/sixty-eight-paise-in-the-rupee/) — Federalism & the Northeast, 8 March 2026, 9 min read. North-eastern and Himalayan states raise roughly a third of what they spend. The problem is not the dependence — it is that most of the money arrives with someone else’s conditions attached.
- [The Half That Does Not Show Up — India's Female Participation Problem](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-half-that-does-not-show-up/) — Work & Livelihoods, 5 March 2026, 9 min read. Female labour force participation has risen to 40%. Urban female participation sits near 25%, and 44.4% of women outside the workforce name care work as the reason. The constraint is not ambition.
- [The Title Is the Asset — Why Indian Land Cannot Be Used as Capital](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-title-is-the-asset/) — Political Economy, 26 February 2026, 11 min read. India's land records are presumptive, not conclusive. A landholding you cannot prove you own is a landholding you cannot borrow against, sell cleanly, or defend in court.
- [Twenty Years After Prakash Singh — The Reform That Was Ordered and Never Delivered](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/twenty-years-after-prakash-singh/) — State Capacity, 19 February 2026, 6 min read. The Supreme Court directed seven police reforms in 2006. Two decades on, forces run at roughly a fifth understrength and 86% of the state police is constabulary with one promotion in a career.
- [The Country That Stopped Counting Itself](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-country-that-stopped-counting-itself/) — Institutions & Reform, 12 February 2026, 8 min read. India's last census was in 2011. Every welfare list, every seat allocation and every per-capita figure in public use rests on a population that no longer exists.
- [The Participation That Is Not Yet Employment](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-participation-that-is-not-yet-employment/) — Work & Livelihoods, 8 February 2026, 9 min read. India’s female labour force participation rose eighteen percentage points in six years — the fastest improvement of any major economy. Almost none of it arrived as a wage.
- [The Capex Budget and the Capacity to Spend It](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-capex-budget-and-the-capacity-to-spend-it/) — Political Economy, 5 February 2026, 10 min read. ₹12.22 lakh crore of capital expenditure against a 4.3% deficit. The Union Budget 2026-27 makes a coherent bet — and hands the binding constraint to the states.
- [The Largest Thing India Does Well](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-largest-thing-india-does-well/) — Institutions & Reform, 1 February 2026, 13 min read. India moves 64 crore people through a voting booth in six weeks without serious incident — the most impressive administrative act on earth. Everything surrounding that act is weaker than the act itself.
